overview.text: Constantin Brâncuși (1876–1957) was a Romanian-born sculptor who settled in Paris in 1904 and became a pioneering figure in modern abstract sculpture. Rather than copying appearances, he carved stone or wood and cast bronze into simplified forms meant to suggest a subject’s essential character; he also treated sculptural bases as part of the artwork. His Bird in Space series turns a recognizable bird into an elongated form focused on the sensation of flight, with each version individually adjusted. Brâncuși’s importance extends beyond gallery sculpture: in 1937–38 he created the Târgu Jiu memorial ensemble in Romania, arranging works including the Endless Column and Table of Silence within the city landscape to commemorate those who died defending it during World War I.

key_facts.text: Born in rural Romania, Brâncuși moved to Paris in 1904, where he established his studio and joined avant-garde art circles.
He worked by carving wood or stone and casting bronze; he often made sculptural bases that formed part of the artwork.
The first Bird in Space was made in marble in 1923. Later versions included bronze and plaster, and Brâncuși altered their proportions so that each was distinct.
The Târgu Jiu ensemble, made in 1937–38, includes the Endless Column, Table of Silence, Gate of the Kiss, and Alley of Chairs; it commemorates those who died defending the city during World War I.
The memorial connects works across two parks along a conceptual axis represented by the Avenue of Heroes, bringing sculpture, landscape, and the city together.
